matched_no_numeric_sample.title: Pacquiao-Bradley II - CompuBox Historical Review
matched_no_numeric_sample.text_sample: Manny Pacquiao landed more punches in 10 of 12 rounds and landed the harder punches all fight. Timothy Bradley was the busier fighter, averaging 70 punches thrown per round. Nearly half of Pacquiao's punch output (landed/thrown) occurred in the last minute of each round. Bradley nearly doubled Manny's output in the first minute of each round. Is it possible the fighter's output in that first minute created the illusion in the eyes of judges Duane Ford & C.J. Ross that Pac had to play catchup the last 2 minutes of each round?

matched_no_numeric_sample.title: CompuBox Analysis: Miguel Cotto-Shane Mosley
matched_no_numeric_sample.text_sample: By Bob Canobbio - Miguel Cotto, 27, making the third defense of his WBA welterweight title, nearly a 7-5 favorite over Shane Mosley, 36, a three-time champion in three different weight classes. A crowd of 19,000-plus, the majority of them being Cotto fans, is expected at New York’s Madison Square Garden. In June, before an announced crowd of 20,658 at The Garden, Cotto, bleeding from cuts over his right eye and lower lip, wore down Brooklyn’s Zab Judah, stopping the former two-time champ in round eleven. Cotto outlanded Judah 90-24 in power shots over the last four rounds before dropping him flat on his back early in the eleventh. Judah beat the count, but the fight was stopped after he absorbed several more Cotto power shots. Overall, Cotto (30-0, 25KOs) landed 292 of 683 total punches (43%-68 thrown per round, 10 more per round than the welterweight average). He also landed 44% of his power shots (214 of 481) and landed 39% of his 20 jabs thrown per round. Judah had his moments, rocking Cotto early in round one and again in the second with left uppercuts. Judah, who was also down in round nine, landed 57% of his power shots (the welterweight avg. is 39% landed), but landed just nine per round, throwing 16. He was too preoccupied with Cotto’s relentless head and body attack to mount his own sustained offense. Overall, Judah averaged 46 punches thrown per round.

matched_no_numeric_sample.title: Erislandy Lara vs. Terrell Gausha - CompuBox Historical Review
matched_no_numeric_sample.text_sample: WBA/IBO junior middleweight champion Erislandy Lara landed 49% of his power punches- #3 among CompuBox Categorical leaders. Opponents landed just 19.4% of their total punches- #5 among CompuBox leaders and 10% lower than jr. middle avg. Lara opponents landed 25.5% of their power punches (8 per round- also #5 among CompuBox leaders). United States Olympian Terell Gausha, making a HUGE step up in class, landed 7.1 jabs per round and 51.8% of his power punches. Gausha opponents landed just 29% of their power shots.

matched_no_numeric_sample.title: Joshua vs. Povetkin: CompuBox Historical Review
matched_no_numeric_sample.text_sample: IBF, IBO, WBC, WBA heavyweight champion Anthony Joshua landed 35% of his total punches, while opponents landed 21.2%, giving Joshua a plus/minus rating of +13.8- #3 among CompuBox Categorical Leaders. Joshua also landed 38.9% of his power punches.

matched_no_numeric_sample.title: Mayweather-Pacquiao: CompuBox Historical Review
matched_no_numeric_sample.text_sample: WBC/WBA welterweight champion Floyd Mayweather Jr. is the more accurate puncher (50% of his power shots in last 13 fights), but throws 16 fewer punches per round than WBO welterweight champion Manny Pacquiao, who landed 47% of his power shots in last 12 fights. Floyd's opponents landed just 19% of their total punches and just 24% of their power shots. Pacquiao opponents landed 25% of their total punches and 34% of their power shots. Mayweather +24 rating #1 among active championship caliber fighters. Pacquiao's 19 landed power shots per round #2 behind only Santa Cruz's 23 landed per round.

matched_no_numeric_sample.title: Keith Thurman vs. Danny Garcia - CompuBox Historical Review
matched_no_numeric_sample.text_sample: Keith Thurman and Danny Garcia land and throw similar amount of total punches. Thurman is more accurate with his power punches (48.2% - #4 on The CompuBox Categorical Leaders list). Garcia throws more power shots.

matched_no_numeric_sample.title: Golovkin-Rubio: CompuBox Historical Review
matched_no_numeric_sample.text_sample: WBA/IBO middleweight champion Gennady "GGG" Golovkin is busier, hits harder and has the better chin. GGG doubled up middleweight avg. for jabs landed per round and landed 44% of his power punches. Opponents (Geale, Macklin, Stevens, Adama, Rosado, Ishida) landed just 22% of their total punches, giving GGG a +16 CompuBox plus/minus rating, tied for #3 w/ Santa Cruz and trailing just Mayweather (+25) and Lara (+17). Marco Antonio Rubio's opponents (Spada, Lemieux, Pavlik, Vanda, Chavez Jr.) landed 34% of their power punches.

matched_no_numeric_sample.title: Wilder-Molina: CompuBox Historical Review

Wilder makes his power punches count, averaging 7 landed per round-4 fewer than the hvt.avg, but landed 53%, 11% higher than wgt. class avg. (Oppopnents: Stiverne, Gavern, Scott, Firtha). Molina has a better than avg. jab (6 of 25 landed per round), however, Wilder is a huge step up in class.

matched_no_numeric_sample.title: Inoue vs. Nieves - CompuBox Historical Review
matched_no_numeric_sample.text_sample: Inoue's plus-13.2 plus-minus rating places him sixth among the CompuBox Categorical leaders, as does his 71.6 punches per round. His 24.9 total connects per round is fifth best among world-class fighters tracked by CompuBox but where he really excels is his jabbing. His 37.1 attempts per round in number one in the Categorical leaders while his 9.6 connects per round trails only Gennady Golovkin's 10.6. Nieves can match Inoue in activity, but not in accuracy & power.

policy: CompuBox-authored BoxingScene articles only; unique local date+pair; explicit numeric patterns only. Articles published before the resolved target bout are pre-fight context and never current-fight observations. Historical-review/last-N-fights aggregates published on/after the target bout are available only for later bouts after publication. Post-fight summaries remain separate from full round reports.
